title: Do not invent a universal bid-change percentage when the account has no sizing policy
scenario: A mature keyword is materially above its target ACOS and the directional formula implies a lower raw bid. The account has no declared max-change policy, no calibrated same-entity bid-response history, and a placement modifier was changed recently. The analyst must not turn the gap into a repository-default percentage cut merely to produce a precise proposed bid.

forbidden_behaviors: Apply a repository-default 20 percent bid cut because no account-specific sizing constraint is available.
Treat the raw bid formula result as an immediately action-safe proposed bid.
Invent a damping factor or max-change percentage without identifying its policy, calibrated history, or experiment basis.
Ignore the still-pending placement change when sizing the base-bid action.
required_observations: The raw bid is an economic/directional anchor, not proof that the full gap should be applied immediately.
Concrete action magnitude needs an explicit account/caller policy, calibrated response evidence, declared experiment design, or another defensible constraint.
The recent placement change couples with base-bid effects and reduces actionability until it is evaluated or the new bid is isolated experimentally.
The result should preserve direction while avoiding false precision when no safe numeric bound is established.

rubric.requirement: Do not manufacture a numeric bid cut from a repository-wide percentage heuristic.
Treat the pending placement change as a coupled-control limitation.
Keep the raw ACOS-derived bid separate from the final allowed action magnitude.
Return a clear directional/Hold/Experiment/Manual Review outcome and name the sizing evidence or policy that is missing.
